Myeongdong BBQ Chicken & Beer: A “Chimaek” Experience That Will Be Etched in Your Memory

By: Witty A.

Rating: ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (5/5 Stars)
In the vibrant, bustling heart of Myeongdong, a district saturated with culinary options, it takes something truly extraordinary to stand out. Today, I found that standout gem: Myeongdong BBQ Chicken & Beer. This establishment delivers a "Chimaek" (chicken and beer) experience that transcends all expectations.
The Chicken: An Edible Work of Art
Let me be clear: the fried chicken here is a phenomenon. From the very first bite of their signature fried chicken, the only word that came to mind was "wow." The golden skin is fried to absolute, shattering perfection, yet the meat within remains unbelievably juicy and tender. The masterful seasoning penetrates deep into the chicken, making every single bite an explosion of balanced and unforgettable flavor. This isn't just fried chicken; it's a culinary masterpiece crafted with precision and passion.
The Beer: The Perfect Partner
The house beer is the perfect counterpart to the rich, savory chicken. Its subtle sweetness and crisp, refreshing character elevate the chicken's flavor while expertly cutting through its richness. It's a thoughtful and flawless pairing that completes the dining experience.
Quality & Service: Excellence in Every Aspect
Beyond the phenomenal taste, the quality of the ingredients is evident in every bite. From the freshness of the chicken to the quality of the side dishes, everything is clearly top-tier.
However, what truly elevates this restaurant is the service. The staff is simply impeccable. Every employee is brimming with a warm smile, providing service that is enthusiastic, attentive, and incredibly efficient. They make you feel quietly welcomed, a quality that is a rare find in such a busy district.
Verdict:
Myeongdong BBQ Chicken & Beer is not just a restaurant; it is an experience. If you are searching for the pinnacle of fried chicken in Seoul, complemented by excellent beer and heartwarming service, look no further. I give this establishment my highest and most enthusiastic recommendation. It has secured a permanent spot on my list of global favorites, and I am certain it will on yours, too.

Since the Chuseok holiday was long, I went out to Myeongdong for the first time in a long time. Whether it was 10 or 20 years ago, you can always see a lot of foreigners in the Myeong-dong commercial district.

This is the worst house in Myeongdong.
Even though there are no ingredients, they take the order and make it poorly.
The ramen was undercooked and the kimbap was like hard steamed rice and not seasoned. Teokbokki is cold. The fish cake was given cold and not boiled. When I complained, they reheated it in hot water, but it wasn't the fish cake we knew.

Food/service/hygiene were all the worst.

They said that if you order at the counter on the first floor, pay, and go up the stairs to the second floor, your food will be delivered in the elevator. When you go up to the second floor, there is a food elevator to the left of the stairs.

When I went to the second floor, there was a team of 2 foreigners, a team of 5 foreigners, a team of 2 Koreans, and the 3 of us.
The table wasn't cleared, so we moved our dishes to the table next to us and sat down.
When I looked around, there was no food on any table. After 5 minutes, a lady from below came up and asked if I wanted food for the elevator.
But I couldn't tell if there was food in the elevator or not. There was no sound in the elevator saying food had arrived, and there was no ding-dong license plate, so how would you know??
The lady gave it to us roughly, but our team, which arrived last, came out first. Everyone said it was strange. My friend ordered one fish cake and while eating it, he looked strange and said he wanted raw fish cake, so he went downstairs, complained, and asked for it to be boiled. It is said that the fish cakes that came out later were not cooked that well.
A foreigner at the next table just ate two cold fish cakes.ㅠ.ㅠ
The food came all at once and the lady came and handed out the tasteless food. Afterwards, 1 out of 5 foreigners lingered around with the receipt saying that no food was served, but the chef came later and told us that the tuna kimbap was for the table next to us, so he ordered us to pay for regular kimbap again. Wow
They paid for the food by mistake and made a foreigner who couldn't communicate with them pay for the food.
Even after I left, I thought that places like this should absolutely disappear.
There was a picture of kimbap and ramen in the picture in front of me, so I thought it was Wooyoungwoo kimbap, and it seemed like a Korean foreigner was coming, but I was so angry that I had to pay first and not be able to leave, but was treated very poorly and had to eat bad food before leaving.
I went out to Myeongdong for the first time in a year, but as expected, I didn't have the same vibe as before, and I was just upset by the odd business.

I absolutely recommend Yehwadang!!!

Donga store. After receiving a recommendation, I stopped by Donga Store a while ago and before moving to the office. After visiting, I wished I had come a few more times.

After thinking about it, I ordered spicy tteokbokki and fried tofu kimbap. What was unique was that they made tteokbokki and kimbap upon ordering. When I asked if it was because there was no one there, they said that all the food was made immediately after ordering.

The tteokbokki that was made right away felt like home-made tteokbokki. It wasn't spicy, but it was quite spicy, and although it was rough, it had plenty of rich seasoning, so eating it with soft wheat rice cake suited my taste. It reminded me of Shinsungdang in Cheongju.

The kimbap with plenty of fried tofu was also good. The warm and sweet taste of tofu went well with the rustic tteokbokki seasoning. The owner, who was watching me enjoy the kimbap, said that he did not initially add tofu to the kimbap, but added it after thinking about it and improving it.

Although the male owner's cooking style seemed rough, it was an attractive snack bar.

After eating everything, I thought that if I ever go back to Euljiro, I should stop by often and try other menu items. I had a good time.

Visited during lunch time on September 30, 2025

I was watching a TV show called ‘Pizza Bread Sandwich’ and I really wanted to try the golden brown bread. Without realizing it, I searched at lightning speed and found myself at the bell tower. It's a long enough distance to go. I thought I had to go before the holidays started, so I decided to do it right away.

Arrived in front of Pajak at 11:40. Alas, people are buzzing just in front of Pajak...there are already a lot of people waiting. Conflict arose for a moment. Should I wait like this before eating? Then...I came from Incheon on purpose. I entered the waiting list at the kiosk at the entrance, and it was number 6. what?
Everyone is waiting to order and pick. I soon sat down on a chair indoors and waited, but I never thought I would be waiting for almost 30 minutes. People next to me said they also waited for about 20 minutes. It is said that there are always this many people on weekdays.

Since I had to eat it to take away, I ordered a dry jambong and cheese sandwich. You order using the QR on the table and pay with your phone. I couldn't pay by phone, so I went to the counter and paid for my order.

The sauce on the jambong and cheese sandwich is so sweet that it takes away from the taste. When I eat it after removing the sauce, it is light and very delicious. I think the bread tastes good even if you just eat it. I enjoyed it with coffee and packed the rest. I walked here and there and had an afternoon snack on a bench in the grass field of the Museum of Modern Art.
The weather was so nice that it was perfect for walking. After lunch at Pajak, we walked along Insadong-gil, Gamgodang-gil, and finished exploring delicious restaurants. I want to go again, but I don't want to wait. I tried it once and am satisfied.

A branch located at the corner of Jongno 2-ga intersection where Jongno and Samil-daero meet. Although Burger King's first branch in Korea was not located in this location, it inherited the name of the Jongno branch after the first branch closed.

Although it has now decreased significantly, the entire building is still in use and remains in place due to the large floating population and the symbolism of the first store. While Burger King remained in place, McDonald's, KFC, and Lotteria closed one after another across the street.

As many as six kiosks are installed on the first floor, so there is no waiting for orders even during peak hours. However, this store does not have an elevator, so tables are set up on the 2nd and 3rd floors, and restrooms are only on the 3rd floor.

Due to the nature of the region, the service speed is quite fast, and as a result, more employees work than other stores. There is no parking lot, and since it is located at an intersection where two roads meet, it is very difficult to stop for a while, so visiting by car is almost impossible.

I am writing this for the store owner to see.

I visited the store during lunch time and ordered, and it took 40 minutes for the food to come out after ordering. Lunch time was almost over, so I finished my food in 5 minutes and had to throw away all the French fries.

When I looked around the store, all the seats were full, 90% of them were waiting for their food, 10% were eating their food, and everyone was eating as fast as I was, as if lunch time was coming to an end.

As I was leaving, I looked at the pickup stand and saw that there was a mountain of pickup orders for delivery.

I got even more angry when I saw that.

Why does the store exist?
Shouldn’t we give priority to customers who visit our store? Otherwise, what is the difference between a delivery company that sets up a space in a quiet basement and only accepts deliveries?

When customers wait for tens of minutes, is it common sense to continue accepting delivery orders and making sales?

If you don't want to give your customers an unpleasant experience, please make improvements.
